dataset_name: Palm Mind AI - Conversational RAG Benchmark
description: A starter evaluation set based only on the supplied Machine Learning and AI Reference Notes. Includes single-turn retrieval, multi-turn follow-ups, and out-of-scope abstention tests.
source_corpus: Machine Learning and AI Reference Notes supplied by the user

schema_notes.query: The exact user message for this turn.
schema_notes.chat_history: Prior conversation messages to provide to the conversational RAG system.
schema_notes.standalone_query: Expected context-independent rewrite. Use this to evaluate query rewriting.
schema_notes.expected_context: Relevant source sentence(s); empty for unanswerable questions.

items.query: What is supervised learning?
items.standalone_query: What is supervised learning?
items.expected_answer: Supervised learning trains a model on labeled examples where every input has a known target output.
expected_context: Supervised learning trains a model on labeled examples where every input has a known target output.

items.query: How does unsupervised learning work?
items.standalone_query: How does unsupervised learning work?
items.expected_answer: Unsupervised learning discovers hidden structure in unlabeled data, for example by grouping similar points into clusters.
expected_context: Unsupervised learning discovers hidden structure in unlabeled data, for example by grouping similar points into clusters.

items.query: What is the difference between semi-supervised and self-supervised learning?
items.standalone_query: What is the difference between semi-supervised and self-supervised learning?
items.expected_answer: Semi-supervised learning combines a small amount of labeled data with a large amount of unlabeled data. Self-supervised learning creates training labels from raw data, such as predicting a masked word.
expected_context: Semi-supervised learning combines a small amount of labeled data with a large amount of unlabeled data during training.
Self-supervised learning creates its own training labels from the raw data, such as predicting a masked word in a sentence.

items.query: What does an agent learn in reinforcement learning?
items.standalone_query: What does an agent learn in reinforcement learning?
items.expected_answer: An agent learns to choose actions using rewards for good outcomes and penalties for bad ones.
expected_context: Reinforcement learning trains an agent to choose actions by giving rewards for good outcomes and penalties for bad ones.

items.query: Define precision and recall.
items.standalone_query: Define precision and recall.
items.expected_answer: Precision is the fraction of predicted positive cases that are correct. Recall is the fraction of real positive cases that the model successfully identifies.
expected_context: Precision measures the fraction of predicted positive cases that are actually correct.
Recall measures the fraction of real positive cases that the model successfully identified.

items.query: What does the F1 score tell us?
items.standalone_query: What does the F1 score tell us?
items.expected_answer: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, balancing the two into one metric.
expected_context: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, balancing the two into a single number.

items.query: Which four outcomes are counted in a confusion matrix?
items.standalone_query: Which four outcomes are counted in a confusion matrix?
items.expected_answer: A confusion matrix counts true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives.
expected_context: A confusion matrix is a table that counts true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives.

items.query: What is the ROC curve plotting?
items.standalone_query: What is the ROC curve plotting?
items.expected_answer: The ROC curve plots the true positive rate against the false positive rate at different decision thresholds.
expected_context: The ROC curve plots the true positive rate against the false positive rate at different decision thresholds.

items.query: Explain overfitting in machine learning.
items.standalone_query: Explain overfitting in machine learning.
items.expected_answer: Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes training data, including noise, and performs poorly on new examples.
expected_context: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes the training data including its noise and fails on new examples.

items.query: How are L1 and L2 regularization different?
items.standalone_query: How are L1 and L2 regularization different?
items.expected_answer: L1 regularization can drive some weights exactly to zero, producing sparse models. L2 regularization smoothly shrinks weights toward zero but rarely makes them exactly zero.
expected_context: L1 regularization, also called Lasso, drives some weights exactly to zero and produces sparse models.
L2 regularization, also called Ridge, shrinks weights smoothly toward zero but rarely makes them exactly zero.

items.query: What is dropout used for?
items.standalone_query: What is dropout used for?
items.expected_answer: Dropout randomly disables a fraction of neurons during training to reduce overfitting in neural networks.
expected_context: Dropout randomly disables a fraction of neurons during training to reduce overfitting in neural networks.

items.query: What does the learning rate control?
items.standalone_query: What does the learning rate control?
items.expected_answer: The learning rate controls the size of each parameter update step during optimization.
expected_context: The learning rate controls how large each parameter update step is during optimization.

items.query: How does backpropagation calculate gradients?
items.standalone_query: How does backpropagation calculate gradients?
items.expected_answer: Backpropagation computes gradients by applying the chain rule backward through the network layers.
expected_context: Backpropagation computes gradients by applying the chain rule backward through the network layers.

items.query: What is the vanishing gradient problem?
items.standalone_query: What is the vanishing gradient problem?
items.expected_answer: It occurs when gradients shrink toward zero, causing early layers to stop learning effectively.
expected_context: The vanishing gradient problem occurs when gradients shrink toward zero so early layers stop learning.

items.query: What makes an LSTM different from a basic RNN?
items.standalone_query: What makes an LSTM different from a basic RNN?
items.expected_answer: An LSTM adds gates to a recurrent network so it can remember information over long sequences.
expected_context: Long short-term memory networks add gates to a recurrent network so it can remember information over long sequences.

items.query: What is self-attention?
items.standalone_query: What is self-attention?
items.expected_answer: Self-attention lets each token in a sequence weigh the importance of every other token when forming its representation.
expected_context: Self-attention lets each token in a sequence weigh the importance of every other token when forming its representation.

items.query: What is cosine similarity and what does it ignore?
items.standalone_query: What is cosine similarity and what does it ignore?
items.expected_answer: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their magnitude.
expected_context: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their magnitude.

items.query: How is Euclidean distance different from cosine similarity?
items.standalone_query: How is Euclidean distance different from cosine similarity?
items.expected_answer: Euclidean distance measures straight-line distance between two points, while cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores magnitude.
expected_context: Euclidean distance measures the straight-line distance between two points in vector space.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their magnitude.

items.query: What does approximate nearest neighbor search trade off?
items.standalone_query: What does approximate nearest neighbor search trade off?
items.expected_answer: Approximate nearest neighbor search trades a little accuracy for much faster retrieval in large vector sets.
expected_context: Approximate nearest neighbor search trades a little accuracy for much faster retrieval in large vector sets.

items.query: Compare bagging and boosting.
items.standalone_query: Compare bagging and boosting.
items.expected_answer: Bagging trains models on random subsets in parallel and averages predictions to reduce variance. Boosting trains models sequentially, with each new model focusing on errors made by the previous one.
expected_context: Bagging trains many models on random subsets of the data in parallel and averages their predictions to reduce variance.
Boosting trains models sequentially where each new model focuses on the errors made by the previous ones.
